description: Absolute docs.honua.io URLs that product code and shipped configuration hand to an operator or an agent at runtime. These are contracts, not prose cross-links: a typed refusal's remediationRef, a SCIM documentationUri, a Prometheus runbook_url. Nothing else notices when the heading underneath one is renamed, so scripts/ci/check-doc-links.py resolves every entry back to a real file and heading in docs/ and fails the gate when it cannot. Adding a new docs.honua.io URL to a scanned source root without registering it here is also an error.

sourceScan.comment: Roots swept for unregistered docs.honua.io URLs. Deliberately narrow: code and shipped config, not documentation prose. Prose cross-links between docs pages are relative and are graded by the relative-link sweep instead.

references.why: SCIM ServiceProviderConfig documentationUri. Advertised on the wire to every SCIM client that discovers the endpoint.

remediationRef on the typed dependency-unavailable refusal (OGC API Processes problem+json, GeoServices error details, MCP error data). An agent is expected to follow this URL to learn how to make the request succeed, so a moved heading is a product defect, not a docs nit.
references.pendingNote: The heading exists only on feat/redis-optional-degraded-receipt. Warn-until-present: the gate stays green on trunk today and enforces the reference the moment #3583 lands. DROP THIS MARKER IN THE SAME PR THAT LANDS #3583 — once the heading resolves, a leftover marker is a hard error, because a warn-forever escape hatch is how a reference quietly stops being enforced.

references.why: runbook_url for HonuaDbPoolUtilizationHigh, HonuaDbPoolUtilizationCritical, HonuaDbConnectionFailures. Retargeted from the dead /operations/runbook#database-connection-issues (#3592).

runbook_url for the memory and query-latency alerts. The section's symptom table covers working-set growth, container OOM, and high latency against a healthy database. Retargeted from /operations/runbook#memory-and-gc-issues and #general-troubleshooting (#3592).

runbook_url for the error-rate alerts and for HonuaServiceDown. Quick triage names the liveness/readiness probes and GET /api/v1/admin/observability/errors, which is the first real step for both. Retargeted from /operations/runbook#general-troubleshooting and #emergency-procedures (#3592).
references.partialGap: HonuaServiceDown gets a correct first step but not the archived runbook's emergency procedures (graceful/forced restart, connection termination, read-only maintenance). Tracked in #3592.

references.why: runbook_url for the upload-queue alerts. The Imports table covers rejected uploads, queue limits, and imports that never progress because Redis is absent. Retargeted from /operations/runbook#file-upload-problems (#3592).

runbook_url for HonuaRateLimitViolationsHigh. Deliberately fragment-less: no live operate or deploy page documents rate-limit incident response, and inventing a heading here would be worse than landing on the troubleshooting index. Gap tracked in #3592.
references.gap: No 'Rate limiting' heading exists. The only live statements are that application-level rate limiting is deferred and must be enforced at the edge (guides/secure/production-checklist.md, reference/configuration/environment-variables.md). See #3592.

references.why: runbook_url for the cache-hit-ratio alerts. The section is the canonical description of the edge/Redis/in-memory cache stack and the fallback behaviour a low hit ratio implies. Retargeted from /operations/runbook#cache-performance-problems (#3592).

runbook_url for RedisDown. The section states exactly what stops working without Redis (durable jobs, queued imports, workflow runs return 503) and what falls back safely. Retargeted from /operations/runbook#cache-performance-problems (#3592).

runbook_url for HonuaCircuitBreakerOpen. The section documents the per-service circuit breakers, their HttpResilience__ knobs, and the circuit-breaker-open troubleshooting entry. Retargeted from /operations/runbook#circuit-breaker-incidents (#3592).
runbook_url for the Redis memory and latency alerts. Deliberately fragment-less: nothing in the live docs covers Redis memory sizing, eviction policy, or latency budgets. Gap tracked in #3592.
references.gap: No 'Redis capacity and latency' heading exists. guides/deploy/backup-and-restore.md documents the durable-job loss contract, which is about Redis loss rather than Redis pressure. See #3592.
